claim.quote: Evidence for the 2π Decay of the K20 Meson

date.note: Publication date; the Letter was received on 10 July 1964.

key_value.quote: a small but non-negligible fraction – 0.2% – of two-body decays into a pair of pions

name: Evidence for the 2π Decay of the K20 Meson
notes: Typed evidence because the Letter's title says "Evidence" (A16); the Nobel citation and BNL call the same work a discovery of CP violation.

summary.plain: Christenson, Cronin, Fitch and Turlay found that the long-lived neutral kaon sometimes decays into two pions, something forbidden if matter and antimatter behaved exactly alike. It was the first sign that nature treats matter and antimatter differently.
summary.technical: Two-pion decays of K_L at about 0.2% of all decays, found with a two-arm spark-chamber spectrometer in a neutral beam at the Brookhaven AGS; interpreted as CP violation.

title: Evidence for the 2π Decay of the K20 Meson
why_it_matters: The 1980 Nobel Prize in Physics went to James Cronin and Val Fitch "for the discovery of violations of fundamental symmetry principles in the decay of neutral K-mesons".
